explanations: The timeout callback in reserve() sets settled and rejects but never calls this.events.off(channel, onRestock). Every reservation that times out leaves its listener (and its closure over sku, qty, resolve/reject) attached to the long-lived emitter. For a SKU that stays out of stock, listeners pile up forever; setMaxListeners(0) silences the warning that would normally flag this, and each later restock event invokes every dead listener (they return early, but are still retained and called). The fix is to remove the listener in the timeout path too.

EventEmitter.emit calls every listener on the channel. Each onRestock calls repo.decrement; only the one whose decrement returns true resolves and removes itself, the others stay registered. emit does not stop after one handler, waiters are not resolved without a successful decrement, and there is no dependence on a later reserve() call.

Node warns when more than 10 listeners attach to one event name; setMaxListeners(0) disables that limit, allowing many waiters per SKU without warnings. It does not change emit timing, does not cap listeners at one, and does not make listeners one-shot (that is once()).

Lines are reserved one by one; nothing releases A's decrement when B fails. The catch block handles StockUnavailableError by calling markBackordered(orderId, err.sku) and returning false. There is no transaction, B is never decremented, and the error is not rethrown.
